sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve

announcements.name: Claude on Azure
announcements.shortDescription: Anthropic's Claude (including Opus 4.8 [inferred], launched the prior week) is now running natively on Azure on GB300 hardware
announcements.longDescription: Anthropic's Claude is now running natively on Azure, on GB300 hardware [inferred] (described as Microsoft's highest-end available hardware). The newest model, Opus 4.8, was launched the prior week and is available in the Foundry model catalog. This brings the Anthropic lifecycle and development tools directly to customers from Azure.

announcements.name: Microsoft first-party models live in Foundry
announcements.shortDescription: New MAI models, including MAI-Image 2.5 [inferred], went live during the morning keynote, spanning image, code, and audio for a full multimodal stack
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced new first-party MAI models during the morning keynote with Mustafa, and the team pushed them live during the session. These models span image, code, and audio, forming a full multimodal application stack. The speaker highlighted MAI-Image 2.5 [inferred] as one of the latest models, emphasizing efficient running and cost optimization.

announcements.name: Aurora 1.5
announcements.shortDescription: A geospatial weather-modeling system using satellite imagery and atmospheric data that scales beyond traditional models
announcements.longDescription: Aurora 1.5 is the newest purpose-built geospatial weather-modeling system highlighted in the Foundry catalog. It uses satellite imagery and atmospheric data and is positioned as cutting-edge, able to scale out where traditional models can't. It is presented as an example of domain-specific, purpose-built models for areas like geospatial, robotics, biomedical, and material science.

announcements.name: Expanded NVIDIA partnership
announcements.shortDescription: Adding Nemotron [inferred] reasoning models, Cosmos for physical AI, and Earth-2 weather models
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA, bringing additional models including Nemotron reasoning models [inferred], Cosmos for physical AI, and the new NVIDIA Earth-2 [inferred] AI weather models. These models enable developers and enterprises to build systems that sense, act, and respond to real-world conditions, extending beyond software workloads into physical AI. Together, the companies are enabling a unified platform spanning into physical AI.

announcements.name: Model router governance
announcements.shortDescription: The Foundry model router now supports 28 models (GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5 family, Claude Opus) with automatic failover, and as of today supports policy governance over which models it may select
announcements.longDescription: The Foundry model router automatically analyzes incoming prompts and routes each request to the best model, supporting 28 different models including GPT-5.4, the GPT-5.5 family, and Claude Opus models. It offers automatic failover to improve customer experience and agentic support. Starting today, it adds policy governance so customers can constrain which models the router is allowed to select; future investment will allow customizing and fine-tuning the router itself and bringing in fine-tuned models.

announcements.name: Rubric-based evaluators
announcements.shortDescription: A new evaluator type that auto-generates weighted, multi-dimension scoring rubrics from an agent's definition and trajectories
announcements.longDescription: Announced at the conference, rubric-based evaluators are a new evaluator type in Foundry alongside existing prompt- and code-based custom evaluators. When creating a rubric evaluator, you select a specific agent, and Foundry analyzes the agent's definition and seeding trajectories to automatically generate a weighted, multi-dimension scoring rubric (e.g., 7 dimensions for the concierge starter travel agent). Users can edit dimension weights, run the evaluation to see successes and failures across dimensions, and perform cluster analysis of results.

announcements.name: Explicit prompt caching / Azure context cache
announcements.shortDescription: A customer-owned cache for guaranteed performance and better privacy, in private preview today
announcements.longDescription: Explicit prompt caching is a new service in Foundry that evolves caching from a low-level optimization into a core system capability, delivering consistent and guaranteed performance and savings. Unlike implicit caching owned by the inference provider, the Azure context cache is owned by the customer—it is your data, with visibility into deployments and savings, providing better privacy controls and better operational availability across long-running tasks. It is available in private preview today.

announcements.name: Serverless reinforcement fine-tuning API
announcements.shortDescription: Launching at Build, giving control over rewards and hyperparameters while Foundry manages infrastructure
announcements.longDescription: Foundry is launching a serverless API at Build that gives users control over their rewards and hyperparameters while Foundry handles the underlying infrastructure with no cluster management required. It produces a set of low-rank weights (LoRA [inferred]) that are overlaid on top of existing deployments. This sits among Foundry's post-training options between managed fine-tuning and full-control RL, the latter allowing full ownership of code, distributed strategies, algorithms, and GPU clusters with frameworks like Slime [inferred].

announcements.name: Fireworks general availability
announcements.shortDescription: GA partnership providing zero-day access to optimized frontier models with native Azure integration
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced the general availability of its partnership with Fireworks for deploying customized and open-source models in Foundry. It brings customers zero-day access to optimized frontier models, best-in-class inferencing performance, and native integration into Azure for an enterprise foundation. The key differentiation versus using Fireworks directly is that on Foundry it deeply integrates across the enterprise stack, using the same auth, API endpoints, and SDK.
